target_customer: Entrepreneurs and small brands launching subscription box businesses, plus consumers who buy boxes on its marketplace
problem: Launching a subscription box business required stitching together storefront, recurring billing and shipping logistics, and new boxes had no audience.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform fees plus marketplace commission

founders.name: Amir Elaguizy
founders.background_notes: Education not listed on the YC page. Described as a software engineer in Austin press.

founders.name: Alex Morse
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in Silicon Hills News and CMS Critic coverage; not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A storefront with recurring billing and shipping integrations built on standard web stack in 2013 to 2014; the YC page and press describe a no-code platform rather than novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Merchants who built on the platform found it hard to move off later per one review, and the marketplace gave exposure, but general commerce tools could be adapted to subscriptions.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: General-purpose commerce platforms and subscription apps were later listed as alternatives by review sites; Cratejoy cut 18 of 43 staff in October 2018 and stayed independent.

market_need_then: Subscription boxes were growing quickly in 2014; Crunchbase data cited in a 2018 report showed funding into the category later fell off. Demand evidence at founding is only the founders' own pivot toward turnkey software after several iterations.

identity.visual_style: Playful consumer marketplace look on the marketplace pages
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly and gift oriented on the marketplace

brand_strength.rationale: No source found on brand impact beyond its marketplace presence; the company published naming advice for subscription businesses but nothing about its own brand.

outcome_analysis: Cratejoy raised a seed round and a 2014 Series A of 4 million dollars led by CRV, riding the subscription box boom. By October 2018 it cut 18 of 43 employees in a restructuring as funding into subscription boxes dried up, but it remains active with 51 staff on the YC page. It stalled below venture scale after the category cooled.
notes: Founding year conflict: YC page says 2014 while the YC batch is Summer 2013; one directory says 2013. TechCrunch 2018 says 10 million dollars raised in total versus 6.2 million in the 2014 VentureBeat report, so later rounds are missing; the company profile mentions an A-1 from A Capital and an aggregator lists a Series A extension in 2015-05, unverified and not recorded as rounds. The Signalbase headline of 4.5 million is unverified. No dated competitor source near 2013 was found, so the list is empty; Subbly and Shopify apps appear only in undated or later comparison pages.
